title: Rear Brake Disc Shield Removal and Installation
introduction:
The brake disc is the rotating surface the pads clamp; the shield sits behind it. I use the illustration to keep those parts straight: the blue panel is the shield, while the wheel hub remains in place. Getting to that panel is a layers-of-an-onion job: wheel, caliper assembly, disc, then shield.

This repair includes the linked brake-disc, wheel and lifting requirements below. Read the installation details before starting, especially the caliper bolts that must be replaced. The final brake-pedal check belongs to the job just as much as removing the shield.

items.name: Prevent unexpected starting
items.detail: Before working around or underneath the vehicle, disable remote start, if equipped, through the Central Display at Vehicle settings > Remote Start Setup. Otherwise, someone could remotely start the vehicle, causing personal injury or death. Switch the ignition OFF and remove the key from the vehicle to prevent another person from starting the engine during service; an accidental start can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Wear protection
items.detail: Wear eye and ear protection while servicing the vehicle, and protective gloves when handling sharp-edged parts such as the shield. Failure to use this protection can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Equipment and materials
items.detail: Have a suitable hoist, a hanger to support the caliper and anchor plate assembly, a wire brush, replacement caliper and anchor plate retaining bolts, and torque equipment suitable for the different fasteners. The [Brake Disc reference](#/document/G1693754) specifies Motorcraft Brake Parts Cleaner — VOC Compliant / Motorcraft Metal Brake Parts Cleaner (PM-4-A, PM-4-B). The [Wheel and Tire reference](#/document/G1686507) specifies Motorcraft High Temperature Nickel Anti-Seize Lubricant (XL-2).

items.name: Chemical handling
items.detail: Read the material safety information sheet before using the specified cleaner or lubricant; misuse can cause serious personal injury. Keep solvents away from ignition sources because they can ignite or explode and cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Hoist setup
items.detail: The wheel-removal procedure calls for the vehicle in NEUTRAL on a hoist. Use a hoist rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications, and position its arms at the locations shown in Jacking and Lifting - Overview. Locate the stamped triangles that identify the lifting points. Lifting elsewhere can let the vehicle shift or fall, causing serious personal injury. Incorrect hoist-arm positioning can cause unintended movement and serious personal injury or death. Do not use the engine to power the drive wheels unless all drive wheels are off the ground.

items.name: Protect the underbody
items.detail: Position hoist adapters clear of suspension, exhaust and steering linkage components. With a two-column hoist, keep the forks clear of suspension components, mounting brackets and stabilizer mounting brackets, if equipped, and avoid damage to the axle or rear cover. Check underbody clearance before entering a drive-on lift. Do not apply jack pressure to either bumper; bumper-cover damage will occur.

items.name: If a jack is used during handling
items.detail: Use a jack rated for the vehicle's weight, including cargo and modifications, on a hard, level surface at the designated lifting points. Set the parking brake and block every wheel remaining on the ground. After jacking, support the vehicle with floor stands; never get underneath a vehicle supported only by a jack, which can lower unexpectedly. Failure to observe these precautions can cause unintended movement, serious personal injury or death. The vehicle's emergency jack is only for changing a deflated tire; using it for this repair can damage the vehicle.

items.name: Wheel condition and seized nuts
items.detail: If a wheel is cracked, deflate its tire before removing the wheel; otherwise, serious personal injury can result. Do not weld or peen a wheel needing repair: install a new wheel, because such repairs can lead to wheel failure and serious personal injury. Never use heat to free a seized wheel nut; heat can damage the wheel and wheel bearing.

items.name: Control friction dust
items.detail: Review Brake and Clutch Systems Health and Safety Precautions before starting. Do not breathe friction dust or blow it from friction components or storage containers with compressed air. Remove dust using government-approved techniques. Dust exposure can cause cancer, lung disease, skin, eye or respiratory irritation, allergic reactions and other chronic health effects. Seek medical attention or advice if irritation persists. Failure to follow these precautions can cause serious personal injury.

items.name: Support the caliper assembly
items.detail: Keep the brake caliper and anchor plate assembly supported when it is positioned aside, using the hanger arrangement illustrated in the Brake Disc reference. Never let its weight hang from the brake hose; that can damage the hose.

items.name: If brake fluid is handled or spilled
items.detail: Use only clean brake fluid meeting the manufacturer's specification, and never reuse drained fluid. This prevents contamination, component damage and the risk of serious personal injury. Immediately wash any brake-fluid spill on paintwork with cold water.

items.name: Clean mounting faces
items.detail: Before installing the wheel, remove corrosion, dirt and foreign material from its mounting face and the mating hub or brake-disc face. Secure any rotor-to-hub fasteners so they cannot interfere with those faces. Otherwise, wheel nuts can loosen and the wheel can detach while driving, causing loss of control and serious injury or death.

items.name: Keep lubricant in its intended location
items.detail: Apply only a thin coat of the specified anti-seize lubricant at the interface between the wheel pilot bore and hub pilot, as highlighted in the wheel illustration. Keep it off the wheel-to-disc or drum mounting face, wheel studs, wheel nuts, brake pads and disc friction surfaces; contamination can damage components.

items.name: Finish tightening and recheck
items.detail: Fit the wheel and initially tighten its nuts only finger tight. Perform final tightening with the vehicle resting on its tires, using clean, dry stud and nut threads and the illustrated star/cross pattern. Tighten to 150 lb.ft (204 Nm). Skipping the cross pattern can increase brake-disc runout and accelerate brake roughness, shudder and vibration. Retighten the wheel nuts within 160 km (100 mi) after reinstallation: wheels can loosen after initial tightening, risking serious injury.

items.name: Home-garage preparation
items.detail: Do not judge asbestos content by appearance. EPA suggests professional servicing when the material is uncertain. If that is not possible and professional dust-control equipment is unavailable, its home-mechanic guidance describes wet wiping: use a low-pressure fine mist of water or detergent-amended water to wet the brake parts, then wipe them with a cloth. Keep bystanders, food and drinks away.

items.name: Contain dust and waste
items.detail: Do not blow dust with compressed air or clean it with a dry rag, brush or garden hose. Do not use an ordinary vacuum lacking HEPA filtration. Keep contaminated clothing and dust out of the house; change clothes and wash soiled clothing separately. EPA recommends double-bagging asbestos waste and following local disposal rules. Read the full [EPA brake-and-clutch guidance](https://www.epa.gov/asbestos/current-best-practices-preventing-asbestos-exposure-among-brake-and-clutch-repair-0) before starting.

items.name: Keep the instructions distinct
items.detail: This is EPA guidance for home mechanics, not a claim that every brake contains asbestos or that employer OSHA duties apply to your home garage. Ford’s later wire-brush instruction concerns mating-face preparation; it does not replace dust control.

items.name: Before releasing the parking brake
items.detail: With all wheels fully clear of the ground and the vehicle securely supported on the hoist, release the parking brake before removing the rear brake disc.

items.name: Before lowering for final wheel tightening
items.detail: After the removed caliper, any disconnected parking-brake cable and all other parking-brake components are fully refitted, reapply the parking brake before lowering the vehicle. Restore ground-wheel restraints as the tires meet the ground, before final wheel-nut tightening.

edits.text: NOTE: Read the removal steps before starting; they also contain details needed during installation.
edits.why: The tightening information appears alongside removal, so reading ahead prevents an incomplete reassembly.

edits.text:
Remove the rear brake disc to expose the shield.
Refer to: Brake Disc (206-04 Rear Disc Brake, Removal and Installation).
edits.why: Use the linked Brake Disc procedure for access. After completing the lifting preparation, remove the wheel nuts and wheel using Wheel and Tire. Remove the caliper and anchor plate retaining bolts, discard those bolts, and support the assembly aside without loading its hose. Then remove the disc from the hub. The drawings show the caliper assembly in yellow when it is positioned aside and the disc in blue when it is removed. I treat the hose like a connection, never a carrying strap.

edits.text:
Remove the 3 retaining bolts, then remove the brake disc shield.
When reinstalling these bolts, tighten to 106 lb.in (12 Nm).
edits.why: The shield is blue and its retaining bolts are magenta in the illustration. The torque belongs to installation; it is not an instruction to tighten the bolts before removal. Keep the shield fasteners distinct from the caliper assembly fasteners used for access.

edits.text: Install the parts in reverse removal order: refit the shield and tighten its bolts to the installation torque given above, then reinstall the brake disc and the components removed for access. Complete the linked Brake Disc and Wheel and Tire installation requirements.
edits.why: Clean the brake-disc mating surfaces with a wire brush and the cleaner specified in the Brake Disc materials table before fitting the disc. Restore the caliper and anchor plate assembly with new retaining bolts and tighten them to 129 lb.ft (175 Nm); the discarded bolts must not go back in. Reinstall the wheel using the cleaning, lubrication and tightening requirements above. Finally, apply the brake pedal several times to verify correct brake-system operation, as required by the Brake Disc procedure.
